- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; align forecast with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 10-day rolling average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the rebound; anticipate a 1–2% upward correction after 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
